guarantees.claim: en_kmac_datapath, en_key_write, clr_keyidx, kmac_valid, kmac_process, sparse_fsm_error_o default to 0 before being possibly overridden by the case statement.
guarantees.cond: always at the start of the combinational block

guarantees.claim: When st == StKmacIdle, st_err_ct_d is forced to 8'd0.
In StKmacIdle, if kmac_en_i && start_i, st_d moves to StKey; else st_d remains StKmacIdle.
In StKey, en_kmac_datapath and en_key_write are asserted (1).
In StKey, if sent_blocksize, st_d = StKmacMsg, kmac_valid = 0, clr_keyidx = 1; else st_d = StKey, kmac_valid = 1.
In StKmacMsg, if process_i or process_latched, st_d = StKmacFlush and kmac_process = 1; else st_d stays StKmacMsg.
In StKmacFlush, if prim_mubi_pkg::mubi4_test_true_strict(done_i) is true, st_d = StKmacIdle; else st_d stays StKmacFlush.
In StTerminalError, if st_err_ct < 100, st_err_ct_d increments by 1 and sparse_fsm_error_o stays 0; if st_err_ct >= 100, sparse_fsm_error_o becomes 1.
If st matches none of the enumerated states (default case), st_d is forced to StTerminalError and sparse_fsm_error_o is asserted (1).
When lc_escalate_en_i is asserted (lc_ctrl_pkg::lc_tx_test_true_loose true), st_d is unconditionally set to StTerminalError, overriding any case-based output.

assumptions.claim: kmac_en_i and start_i must be held stable and high long enough to be captured by the FSM in the StKmacIdle state.
assumptions.cond: when the FSM is in idle and should start
assumptions.risk: If the start condition is deasserted before the register captures it, the FSM will not transition to StKey, stalling the key-load phase.

assumptions.claim: sent_blocksize must be asserted exactly when a full key block has been transferred to the SHA3 datapath.
assumptions.risk: A premature sent_blocksize causes premature transition to message phase with incomplete key material, leading to incorrect MAC output (security-critical). A delayed or missing assertion stalls the FSM in StKey.

assumptions.claim: process_i and process_latched must be asserted only after all message data has been written to the SHA3 core.
assumptions.risk: Premature assertion moves the FSM to StKmacFlush, truncating the message and producing an incorrect MAC.

assumptions.claim: done_i must be a properly encoded mubi4_true_strict value and asserted only after SHA3 processing completes.
assumptions.risk: A false done_i returns the FSM to idle prematurely, potentially discarding the final digest. A missing done_i hangs the FSM indefinitely in flush state.

assumptions.claim: The state register st must be reset externally to StKmacIdle (or a legal state) before operation.
assumptions.risk: If st contains an illegal value, the FSM immediately enters StTerminalError via the default case and asserts sparse_fsm_error_o, causing a false alarm and loss of function.

assumptions.claim: st_err_ct must be reset to 0 (externally) to ensure consistent error counter start.
assumptions.cond: at reset release or before first use
assumptions.risk: If st_err_ct is 100 or greater when StTerminalError is entered, sparse_fsm_error_o asserts immediately instead of after the intended delay, potentially causing a false escalation spike for error conditions that might be transient.

uncertain_points.claim: When lc_escalate_en_i forces StTerminalError, sparse_fsm_error_o is not asserted immediately but waits up to 100 cycles (depending on st_err_ct). During this window the system may not report the escalation.
uncertain_points.risk: A delayed escalation signal could miss the fault-containment deadline, leaving secret/state unprotected for up to 100 clock cycles.

uncertain_points.claim: The default case (illegal state) asserts sparse_fsm_error_o immediately, whereas entering StTerminalError via lc_escalate_en_i or other explicit paths delays the assertion by up to 100 cycles. The design intent behind this asymmetry is unclear.
uncertain_points.risk: Could indicate a missed security requirement: temporary illegal states might be immediately signaled while deliberate escalations are delayed, possibly under-protecting the deliberate path.

uncertain_points.claim: The correctness of sent_blocksize, process_i, process_latched, and done_i (which govern FSM progression and key/message boundaries) depends on generation logic in other modules. Their timing and protocol must be verified against the assumptions.
uncertain_points.cond: whenever these signals change during operation
uncertain_points.risk: If any of these external signals violates the assumed contract, the KMAC FSM can produce incorrect MAC, leak key material, or stall.
